section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the header and date for the maamar.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Motzaei Shabbos Kodesh Parshas Bo,
Yud Shevat,
the year 5737*

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Midrashic interpretation of "to My garden" and the work of the tzaddikim to draw down the Shechinah, exemplified by the Mishkan made from shittim wood, representing the transformation of folly into holiness.
section.t: "I have come to My garden, My sister, My bride"1,
And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, author of the Yom Tov Shel Rosh HaShanah and the one of the hillula, brings on this in his well-known maamar for Yud Shevat 5710,
that it is stated in Midrash Rabbah2a
"to a garden" is not written here, but rather "to My garden," to My private chamber,
to the place which was My primary [place]
[meaning the primary place of His dwelling]
at first,
that
[at the time of the creation of the world]
the primary dwelling of the Shechinah was in the lower realms,
and through the undesirable matters that occurred afterwards, the Shechinah departed from the earth to the firmament, until it departed to the seventh firmament.
And afterwards, seven tzaddikim arose and brought down the Shechinah below,
beginning with Avraham Avinu who brought down the Shechinah from the seventh firmament to the sixth, until Moshe, who is the seventh,
and all sevenths are beloved4,
brought it down below to the earth.
And this is the entire matter of the service of the tzaddikim,
and "Your people are all tzaddikim"5,
to draw down the Shechinah below,
as it is stated6
"Tzaddikim will inherit the land and dwell forever upon it,"
that the service of tzaddikim is "and they will dwell" – to cause to dwell,
"forever" – the Shechinah,
the aspect of "He Who dwells forever, exalted and holy,"
"upon it" – below on the earth.
And the drawing down of the Shechinah below that was through Moshe was through the work of the Mishkanb,
for its matter is what is stated7
"And they shall make for Me a Sanctuary and I will dwell in their midst,"
in which and through which was the drawing down of the Shechinahc.
And behold, the beginning of the Mishkan was with the planks12,
which they made from shittim wood,
and as it is stated13
"And you shall make the planks for the Mishkan of shittim wood, standing upright."
And the explanation of this is
[as is explained in the maamar there14
based on the Gemara15
and the Midrash16]
that "shittim" is from the term "shtus" (folly),
and it is the folly of idolatry/alien forces,
as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said17
"A person does not commit a transgression unless a spirit of folly enters into him,"
and the service is, through subjugation and transformation, to turn the folly of idolatry/alien forces into the folly of holiness
[as per the statement18
"His folly benefited him, the elder"].
And this is that the planks were of shittim wood,
that through the service of man, one makes from the folly of idolatry/alien forces
(shittim)
planks for the Mishkan.
And this is also the name "kerashim" (planks),
for "keresh" is the letters of "sheker" (falsehood),
except in a different arrangement,
and this means that their matter is that from the falsehood of the world, one makes a plank for the Mishkan,
and through this one establishes
(sets up)
the Mishkan.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the letters Kuf and Reish as letters of falsehood, and how through the yud of the letter Daled, the poverty of holiness (bittul) is distinguished from the poverty of the alien side.
section.t: B)
And he continues that
in the maamar there23

behold, in the introduction to the Zohar regarding the letters that came before the Holy One, blessed be He, to create the world with them, etc., it is stated that the letters Kuf and Reish are letters that appear on the side of evil,
and in order to endure, they take the letter Shin within them, etc.,
for the letter Shin is a letter of truth
(as stated earlier in the Zohar there).
And the reason they needed the letter of truth is because falsehood has no legs, etc.
And the service is to make from this falsehood
(of the letters Kuf and Reish)
planks for the Mishkan,
and this is through the alien forces of these letters.
For "this [letter] God made for the alien forces"24,
and corresponding to the letter Reish
(a letter of falsehood)
in the alien forces,
behold there is a letter Daled in holiness.
For even though Daled and Reish are similar in their interpretation,
for Daled is from the term "dalus" (poverty and lowliness) and likewise the letter Reish is from the term poverty and lowliness,
nevertheless, they are distinct and divided in their matters, to the point that the difference between them is a fundamental difference.
And this is understood from what is stated in the Midrash25
regarding the caution that one must not exchange Daled for Reish and Reish for Daled,
and in these letters is the difference between "Hashem is One" and the matter of an "other god"
[and in the two verses, the Daled and Reish are in large letters],
and when one exchanges a Reish in place of the Daled and a Daled in place of the Reish, this destroys worlds.
From this it is understood that the difference between them is from one extreme to the other.
And the difference between them in their form is
[as explained in the seventh section]
that in the letter Daled there is a small yud
[an aspect of a point]
at its back,
unlike the letter Reish,
and through this yud, in place of the Reish,
which is the matter of the poverty and lowliness of the alien forces,
is made the letter Daled of holiness
(end of the content of section 7 there).
And even though Daled is also from the term poverty and lowliness
(as above),
it is not at all the matter of the poverty of the Reish of the alien forces,
for the matter of the poverty of holiness indicates the matter of bittul (self-nullification) of holiness,
and as it is stated, "And may my soul be like dust to all,"
"For I am poor and needy" etc.26,
for this is the matter of poverty from the aspect of bittul in holiness
[and as is explained at length in the previous section27
the modes and levels of bittul,
up to the bittul of "diminishing oneself"28
and "the moon has nothing of its own"29
– for this bittul of "it has nothing of its own" is bittul to the ultimate degree and in completeness,
even more than the bittul of "diminishing oneself."
For in "diminishing oneself," there still exists an entity,
except that the entity is in an aspect of smallness,
unlike "it has nothing of its own,"
where it has no existence at all
(not even in a manner of smallness)
and it is in the ultimate bittul]
unlike the poverty and lowliness that is in the alien forces, whose matter is as it is stated30
"and the poor has nothing."
And he continues to explain in the maamar31
the matter of the yud that is at the back of the Daled
(through which it is distinguished from the Reish of the alien forces,
which has no yud)
that although it is the smallest of all the letters, nevertheless it is the head of all the letters,
for every letter, its beginning is a letter yud, and it is what
[is stated in the Gemara Menachos32]
that with the yud the World to Come was created
[and from this it is drawn down afterwards into the Sefirah of Yesod
(as will be explained later)]
for about this it says33
"For all in heaven and earth," and Targum renders "Who holds heaven and earth,"
which is the Sefirah of Yesod, from which the aspect of Malchus receives, etc.
(end of the maamar there).
